standard_prerequisites.name: Endomorphism rings and bicommutants
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the definitions of the endomorphism ring of a module and of the bicommutant, and the convention for the module structure over them
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the objects A' and A'' of the proof and the side on which the bicommutant acts.

standard_prerequisites.name: Two-sided ideals and the product ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the elementary theory of two-sided ideals in a ring
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the product of the ring with a nonzero right ideal is a two-sided ideal, and that a ring with no nontrivial two-sided ideal has an injective structural map determined by the identity.

core_obligations: Setup and injectivity (proof lines 316-324): writing A' for the endomorphism ring of the right ideal and A'' for the bicommutant, the author views the ideal as a right module over the bicommutant and introduces the natural homomorphism from the ring to the bicommutant, which is injective because it sends the identity to the identity and the ring has no nontrivial two-sided ideal.

The image of the ideal is a right ideal (proof lines 324-330): for an element of the bicommutant and an element of the ideal, the product of their images is the image of a product, because left multiplication of the module by an element of the ideal represents an element of the endomorphism ring and hence commutes with the bicommutant.

Conclusion (proof lines 330-333): the product ideal of the ring with the nonzero right ideal is a two-sided ideal and therefore equals the ring, so the image of the ring equals the image of the ring times the image of the ideal and hence is a right ideal inside the bicommutant containing the identity of the bicommutant, which forces the two to be equal.
proof_roadmap: Introduce the endomorphism ring and the bicommutant and the natural map between the ring and the bicommutant.
Show the map is injective and that the image of the ideal is a right ideal.
Use that the product ideal is the whole ring to conclude that the image of the ring is the whole bicommutant.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states Rieffel's theorem: for a ring with no nontrivial two-sided ideal and a nonzero right ideal, the ring coincides with the bicommutant of that right ideal (statement lines 308-314). The proof is a complete argument: the natural map from the ring to the bicommutant is shown injective using the absence of nontrivial two-sided ideals (proof lines 316-324); the image of the ideal is shown to be a right ideal in the bicommutant because left multiplication by an element of the ideal is an endomorphism of the module (proof lines 324-330); and since the product ideal is two-sided and hence the whole ring, the image of the ring is a right ideal in the bicommutant containing the identity, which forces equality (proof lines 330-333). The non-formal content is the definition of the module structure on the far side and the two-sidedness argument. The claim is H2.
